\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Tensorization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Tensorization
\section{Overview}
Minkowski for nonnegative product integrals compares mixed norms. Affine contraction for each of two probability laws then passes to their independent sum, including essential-supremum exponents.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Minkowski inequality for nonnegative product integrals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.lintegral_minkowski}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $(A,\mu)$ and $(B,\nu)$ be probability spaces, let $f:A\times B\to[0,\infty]$ be
measurable, and let $r\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le r$. Then $\left(\int_B\left(\int_A
f(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\right)^r d\nu(y)\right)^{1/r}\le\int_A\left(\int_B
f(x,y)^r\,d\nu(y)\right)^{1/r}d\mu(x)$, with the integrals and powers taken in the
nonnegative extended reals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison of mixed nonnegative integrals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.mixed_lintegral_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.lintegral_minkowski}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(A,\mu)$ and $(B,\nu)$ be probability spaces, let $g:A\times B\to[0,\infty]$ be
measurable, and let $p,q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p\le q$. Then $\left(\int_B\left(\int_A
g(x,y)^p\,d\mu(x)\right)^{q/p}d\nu(y)\right)^{1/q}\le\left(\int_A\left(\int_B
g(x,y)^q\,d\nu(y)\right)^{p/q}d\mu(x)\right)^{1/p}$, with integrals and powers taken in
the nonnegative extended reals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-exponent affine sum contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.affine_sum_le_of_ne_top}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.mixed_lintegral_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\mathbb R$, let $p,q\in[0,\infty]$
satisfy $1\le p\le q<\infty$, and let $\rho\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that for each
$\theta\in\{\mu,\nu\}$ and all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the extended $L^p$ and $L^q$ seminorms
satisfy $\|x\mapsto a+\rho bx\|_{L^q(\theta)}\le\|x\mapsto a+bx\|_{L^p(\theta)}$. Then
for all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $\|(x,y)\mapsto a+\rho
b(x+y)\|_{L^q(\mu\times\nu)}\le\|(x,y)\mapsto a+b(x+y)\|_{L^p(\mu\times\nu)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform moment bounds control the essential supremum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.eLpNorm_top_le_of_forall_nat}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $(A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f:A\to\mathbb R$ be almost everywhere strongly
measurable. For $C\in[0,\infty]$ and $N\in\mathbb N$, suppose that $\|f\|_{L^n(\mu)}\le
C$ for every natural number $n\ge N$. Then $\|f\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}\le C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine sum contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.affine_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.affine_sum_le_of_ne_top, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.eLpNorm_top_le_of_forall_nat}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\mathbb R$, let $p,q\in[0,\infty]$
satisfy $1\le p\le q$, and let $\rho\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that for each
$\theta\in\{\mu,\nu\}$ and all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the extended $L^p$ and $L^q$ seminorms
satisfy $\|x\mapsto a+\rho bx\|_{L^q(\theta)}\le\|x\mapsto a+bx\|_{L^p(\theta)}$. Then
for all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $\| (x,y)\mapsto a+\rho
b(x+y)\|_{L^q(\mu\times\nu)}\le\|(x,y)\mapsto a+b(x+y)\|_{L^p(\mu\times\nu)}$.
\end{theorem}
